subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-week-old boy is evaluated for poor feeding, profound hypotonia, and seizures. He was born at term with a prominent forehead, a large anterior fontanelle, and a flat nasal bridge, and he has been jaundiced since the second day of life. Examination shows a floppy infant with hepatomegaly and a high-pitched cry. Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids are elevated and pipecolic acid is also elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Zellweger syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder of peroxisome biogenesis caused by mutations in PEX genes, so peroxisomes never form properly and all peroxisomal functions fail. Patients show hypotonia, seizures, jaundice, craniofacial dysmorphia, hepatomegaly, and early death, with accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids and pipecolic acid. Because peroxisomes cannot assemble, the defect extends beyond a single enzyme pathway and produces a severe, multisystem disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Refsum disease is a single peroxisomal α-oxidation defect that presents in older children or adults with retinitis pigmentosa, anosmia, ataxia, and ichthyosis, not with neonatal dysmorphism.
explanation_incorrect.B: X-Linked adrenoleukodystrophy typically presents in childhood with behavioral decline and adrenal insufficiency; affected patients have peroxisomes but cannot import very-long-chain fatty acids for β-oxidation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a lysosomal arylsulfatase A deficiency producing demyelination without craniofacial dysmorphism or jaundice.
explanation_incorrect.E: Niemann-Pick type A presents later in infancy with hepatosplenomegaly and a cherry-red macular spot due to sphingomyelinase deficiency.

educationalObjective: Neonatal hypotonia, seizures, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatomegaly, and elevated very-long-chain fatty acids indicate Zellweger syndrome, a defect of peroxisome biogenesis.
